newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed's Moskow says not alarmed by PPI rise.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed's Moskow says not alarmed by PPI rise.

text.p: Chicago Federal Reserve Bank president Michael Moskow said Thursday he is not alarmed by the 0.5-percent increase in the U.S. producer price index for December.
"If energy starts to spill over into the cost of goods and services, then it becomes a concern. But we haven't seen that yet," Moskow told reporters following a speech to a business group here.
December PPI rose 0.5 percent overall and gained 0.1 percent in the core rate. Energy prices rose 3.1 percent.

Moskow noted the increase in the PPI energy segment and the small increase in the core PPI inflation rate but declined to be drawn into the recent argument over whether the consumer price index overstates the actual inflation rate.

He reiterated that he was encouraged by the slowing rise in the level of consumer debt, noting that commercial bank loan officers were being more careful about making loans. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
